prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: An animal sanctuary is a special place where rescued, injured, or _______ animals can live in a safe and caring environment.
explanation: abused(학대받은). 보호소는 구조된(rescued)·다친(injured)·학대받은(abused) 동물이 안전하게 사는 곳이다.

prompt: 밑줄 친 sanctuary의 뜻으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
passage: Our club organized a volunteer trip to an animal sanctuary called Free Animals.
explanation: sanctuary는 ‘보호 구역, 안식처’. 동물원(zoo)과 달리 구조·보호가 목적인 곳이다.

prompt: 다음 글의 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: At the sanctuary, the volunteers helped with animal care by (A) _______ habitats and preparing food. They chopped bananas into small pieces for the elderly elephants, which had (B) _______ teeth.
explanation: 봉사 내용은 서식지 청소(cleaning habitats)와 먹이 준비. 나이 든 코끼리는 이가 약해서(weak teeth) 바나나를 잘게 썰어 주었다.

prompt: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As the leader of the Care for Animals club, I planned a trip so that our members could volunteer at an animal sanctuary. We cleaned habitats, prepared food, and learned how much care rescued animals need.
choices: a club's volunteer experience at an animal sanctuary
how to adopt a pet from a shelter
the cost of running a zoo
explanation: 동아리 리더가 기획한 동물 보호소 자원봉사 경험이 글의 중심 내용이다.

prompt: 밑줄 친 habitat의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
passage: Every morning we cleaned the habitats where the rescued animals lived.
explanation: habitat 서식지. habit(습관)과 철자가 비슷하므로 주의.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The elderly elephants have weak teeth, so the volunteers _______ the bananas into small pieces before feeding them.
explanation: chop 잘게 썰다. 이가 약한 나이 든 코끼리가 먹기 쉽도록 바나나를 잘게 썰었다.

prompt: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: I am the leader of our school's animal protection club. This spring, I organized a volunteer trip to Free Animals, a sanctuary for rescued, injured, or abused animals. There, our members cleaned habitats and prepared food. For the elderly elephants with weak teeth, we chopped bananas into small pieces.
choices: 바나나를 잘게 썬 것은 어린 코끼리를 위해서였다.
Free Animals는 구조되거나 다친 동물을 위한 보호소이다.
explanation: 바나나를 잘게 썬 것은 이가 약한 나이 든(elderly) 코끼리를 위해서이다.

prompt: 밑줄 친 단어와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
passage: The staff at the sanctuary take care of more than fifty animals every day.
explanation: take care of = look after 돌보다. look for 찾다, look up 찾아보다, give up 포기하다, put off 미루다.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Even a few hours of volunteering can _______ in the lives of animals in need.
explanation: make a difference 변화를 만들다, 도움이 되다. in need 도움이 필요한.

prompt: 다음 중 단어와 뜻이 잘못 짝지어진 것은?
explanation: caring은 ‘보살피는, 배려하는’이다. ‘부주의한’은 careless.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Many animals arrive at the sanctuary after being _______ from illegal traders.
explanation: rescued 구조된. 불법 거래상으로부터 구조되어 보호소에 온다는 문맥.

prompt: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
passage: ① Volunteering at the sanctuary was harder than we had expected. ② We had to wake up early to clean the habitats. ③ Preparing food for dozens of animals took hours. ④ The sanctuary's gift shop sells T-shirts in three colors. ⑤ Still, seeing the animals eat well made every minute worth it.
explanation: ④는 기념품 가게에 대한 내용으로, 봉사의 힘듦과 보람이라는 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

prompt: 다음 중 5형식(S + V + O + O.C.) 문장은?
choices: She gave me a book about elephants.
explanation: made(V) everyone(O) happy(O.C.) — ‘everyone is happy’의 관계가 성립하므로 5형식. ①은 4형식, ③ 1형식, ④ 2형식, ⑤ 3형식.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: My teacher had us _______ the habitats before lunch.
explanation: 사역동사 have + 목적어 + 동사원형. 목적어(us)가 청소를 하는 능동 관계이므로 clean.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: By the time we arrived at the sanctuary, the staff _______ the food for the animals.
explanation: 우리가 도착한 과거 시점보다 먼저 완료된 일이므로 과거완료 had prepared.

prompt: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: The rescued animals live in a safe environment.
The leader asked us to bring gloves.
He let the volunteers feed the goats.
We kept the habitat clean all day.
She saw the elephant to eat bananas.
explanation: 지각동사 see + 목적어 + 동사원형/-ing. to eat → eat 또는 eating.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When I got to the shelter, the dog I wanted _______ already _______.
explanation: 내가 도착한 과거 시점 이전에 입양이 완료되었고, 개는 입양 ‘되는’ 대상이므로 과거완료 수동 had already been adopted.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We consider volunteering _______ for our community.
explanation: consider + 목적어 + 형용사 보어. 목적어 volunteering을 설명하는 형용사 important.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The staff allowed us _______ the baby goats.
explanation: allow + 목적어 + to부정사. want/ask/tell/allow/expect는 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취한다.

prompt: 밑줄 친 had never seen의 용법으로 알맞은 것은?
passage: I had never seen an elephant up close before I visited the sanctuary.
explanation: 방문한 과거 시점까지 ‘한 번도 본 적이 없었다’는 경험을 나타낸다. never, before가 단서.

prompt: 다음 문장을 5형식으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
passage: The volunteers helped. The elephants ate the bananas.
choices: The volunteers helped eating the bananas the elephants.
The volunteers helped that the elephants ate the bananas.
The volunteers helped the elephants ate the bananas.
The volunteers helped the elephants eat the bananas.
The volunteers helped to the elephants eat the bananas.
explanation: help + 목적어 + (to) 동사원형. ‘helped the elephants (to) eat’이 5형식이다.

prompt: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: I had my bike repaired yesterday.
She made her brother wash the dishes.
He got his friend help him.
We watched the birds flying over the lake.
explanation: get은 사역의 의미라도 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취한다: got his friend to help him.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: She _______ at the sanctuary for three years when she finally decided to adopt a dog.
explanation: 결정한 과거 시점까지 3년간 계속 일해 오고 있었으므로 과거완료 진행 had been working.

prompt: 다음 두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 할 때 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
passage: The sanctuary was so peaceful that it made the visitors _______.  (= The visitors felt relaxed.)
explanation: make + 목적어 + 형용사 보어. 방문객이 ‘편안함을 느끼는’ 상태이므로 과거분사형 형용사 relaxed. relaxing은 ‘편안하게 해 주는’.

prompt: 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
passage: Before we ① left the sanctuary, the manager ② told us ③ to write about what we ④ had learned, so I ⑤ have written this report last night.
explanation: last night는 명확한 과거 시점이므로 현재완료와 함께 쓸 수 없다. have written → wrote.

prompt: 제목 ‘From Shadows to Spotlights’의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 눈에 띄지 않던(무명의) 사람들이 주목받는 자리로 옮겨 갔다.
그림자를 이용한 새로운 미술 기법이 유행한다.
전시장이 어두운 곳에서 밝은 곳으로 이사했다.
유명 화가들이 은퇴 후 조용한 삶을 택했다.
explanation: shadows(그늘·무명·배경)에서 spotlights(주목·명성)로 — 인정받지 못하던 화가들이 세상의 주목을 받게 되는 흐름의 비유.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: During her lifetime, her paintings were _______ by critics, and she sold almost nothing. Today they hang in the world's greatest museums.
explanation: overlook 간과하다, 못 보고 지나치다. 생전에는 비평가들이 무시했지만 지금은 세계적 미술관에 걸려 있다는 대비.

prompt: 밑줄 친 appreciate의 뜻으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
passage: You don't need a degree in art history to appreciate a great painting.
explanation: appreciate 감상하다·진가를 알아보다. 문맥에 따라 ‘고마워하다’의 뜻도 있다.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The painter finally gained _______ for his work only after his death.
explanation: gain recognition 인정을 받다. 사후에야 비로소 작품이 인정받았다는 뜻.

prompt: 다음 중 단어와 뜻이 잘못 짝지어진 것은?
explanation: masterpiece는 ‘걸작’이다.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: His style was so _______ of his time that most people simply could not understand it.
explanation: ahead of one's time 시대를 앞선. 당대 사람들이 이해하지 못한 이유를 설명하는 표현.

prompt: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Talent alone does not bring an artist into the spotlight. Behind almost every artist who was rediscovered, there was someone who kept the paintings, wrote the letters, or organized the first exhibition. These true art lovers changed the story.
choices: 편지를 쓰는 습관이 화가의 실력을 키운다.
미술관은 유명 화가의 작품만 전시해야 한다.
무명 화가가 주목받기까지는 그 가치를 알아보고 알린 사람의 역할이 컸다.
전시회는 비용이 많이 들어 열기 어렵다.
explanation: 재능만으로는 부족하며, 작품을 지키고 알린 ‘진정한 예술 애호가’가 있었다는 것이 요지.

prompt: 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage:
[주어진 문장] Everything changed when a young collector came across one of her canvases in a small shop.

( ① ) For thirty years she painted in a tiny apartment, showing her work to no one. ( ② ) Galleries returned her letters unopened. ( ③ ) He bought the painting, tracked her down, and arranged her first exhibition. ( ④ ) Within a year, critics who had never heard her name were calling her a genius. ( ⑤ )
explanation: ‘He bought the painting’의 He는 주어진 문장의 a young collector를 가리키므로, 그 앞(③)에 들어가야 한다. 그늘 → 전환점 → 주목의 흐름.

prompt: 밑줄 친 표현의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
passage: Hundreds of her drawings came to light only when her family opened an old trunk in the attic.
explanation: come to light 알려지다, 드러나다. 숨겨져 있던 그림들이 세상에 나왔다는 뜻.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: He _______ his whole life to painting, even when no one would buy a single work.
explanation: devote A to B: A를 B에 바치다. 아무도 사 주지 않아도 평생을 그림에 바쳤다.

prompt: 다음 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage:
[주어진 글] Some of the most famous painters in history were almost completely unknown while they were alive.
(A) Years later, a friend or a family member refused to let the work be forgotten and showed it to the world.
(B) Their paintings were rejected by galleries, and they often lived in poverty.
(C) Only then did the public finally see what these true art lovers had seen all along.
explanation: 무명·가난(B) → 가족·친구가 세상에 알림(A) → 그제야 대중이 알아봄(C)의 ‘그늘 → 전환점 → 주목’ 순서.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Her bold use of color _______ a whole generation of younger artists.
explanation: inspire 영감을 주다. 과감한 색 사용이 후배 화가 세대 전체에 영감을 주었다.

prompt: 다음 중 ‘무명’의 상태를 나타내는 표현이 아닌 것은?
explanation: in the spotlight는 ‘주목을 받는’ 상태로, 나머지(그늘에 가려진·대중에게 알려지지 않은·비평가에게 간과된·인정받지 못한)와 반대이다.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Not until years after his death _______ his true talent.
explanation: Not until이 문두에 오면 주절은 ‘조동사 + 주어 + 동사원형’으로 도치. 과거이므로 did people recognize.

prompt: 다음 문장을 도치문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
passage: It was not until 1900 that a gallery agreed to show her paintings.
choices: Not until 1900 a gallery agreed to show her paintings.
Not until 1900 a gallery did agree to show her paintings.
Not until did 1900 a gallery agree to show her paintings.
Not until 1900 agreed a gallery to show her paintings.
Not until 1900 did a gallery agree to show her paintings.
explanation: It was not until A that S + V = Not until A + did + S + 동사원형.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: _______ in poverty for most of his life, the painter never stopped working.
explanation: 주어(the painter)가 ‘사는’ 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 Living. (= Although he lived …)

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: _______ by every gallery in the city, she began selling her paintings on the street.
explanation: 주어(she)가 거절을 ‘당하는’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 Rejected. (Being rejected에서 Being 생략)

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: This is the small town _______ the painter spent his last years.
explanation: 뒤 절(the painter spent his last years)이 완전하므로 관계부사 where (= in which).

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The painting _______ she kept in the attic is now worth millions.
explanation: kept의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이므로 관계대명사 which(that). 선행사 the painting이 있으므로 what ❌.

prompt: 다음 분사구문을 부사절로 바꿀 때 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 접속사는?
passage:
Having no money for paint, he still produced hundreds of drawings.
= _______ he had no money for paint, he still produced hundreds of drawings.
explanation: ‘물감 살 돈이 없었음에도 불구하고’ — still이 단서. 양보의 접속사 Although.

prompt: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: Not until the exhibition opened did critics take her seriously.
This is the studio which the artist painted her masterpiece.
The painter, working alone at night, filled dozens of canvases.
Exhausted but happy, he finished the portrait at dawn.
The letters that his brother kept revealed his struggles.
explanation: ‘the artist painted her masterpiece’는 완전한 절이므로 관계부사 where 또는 in which가 필요하다.

prompt: 다음 두 문장의 뜻이 같도록 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
passage:
I still remember the day when her first exhibition opened.
= I still remember the day _______ her first exhibition opened.
explanation: 관계부사 when = 전치사 + which. 날짜(the day)에는 전치사 on을 쓰므로 on which.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Not until she looked closely _______ the tiny signature in the corner.
explanation: Not until + 절 뒤의 주절은 도치: did she notice. 시제는 looked에 맞춰 과거.

prompt: 밑줄 친 Having painted의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Having painted for thirty years without a single sale, she finally held her first exhibition.
choices: Unless she had painted for thirty years without a single sale
If she paints for thirty years without a single sale
Although she paints for thirty years without a single sale
Because she had painted for thirty years without a single sale
While she will paint for thirty years without a single sale
explanation: Having p.p.는 주절보다 앞선 일을 나타내는 완료 분사구문. ‘30년간 한 점도 못 팔고 그려 온 뒤에’ 첫 전시를 열었다.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: _______ that his work would one day be famous, the painter gave most of it away.
explanation: 분사구문의 부정은 분사 앞에 Not을 둔다: Not knowing (= As he didn't know).

prompt: 다음 문장을 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
passage: While he was traveling through the countryside, he sketched everything he saw.
choices: Traveled through the countryside, he sketched everything he saw.
Being traveled through the countryside, he sketched everything he saw.
To travel through the countryside, he sketched everything he saw.
He traveling through the countryside, he sketched everything he saw.
Traveling through the countryside, he sketched everything he saw.
explanation: 접속사·주어 생략, was traveling → traveling. 능동이므로 현재분사.

prompt: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The reason _______ the galleries rejected her work is hard to understand today.
explanation: 선행사 the reason + 완전한 절 → 관계부사 why (= for which).

prompt: 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
passage: ① Not until the collector visited the shop ② did anyone notice the small canvas ③ hanging near the door, ④ that the old painter had made ⑤ decades earlier.
explanation: 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법에는 that을 쓸 수 없다. that → which.
